newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Dec 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Dec 20.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- GKN FACES DAMAGES OF $554 MILLION OVER US CLAIMS

One of the UK's largest engineering groups, GKN, could be forced to pay damages of up to $554 million (331.7 million stg) after losing a suit involving one of its US car-parts subsidiaries. A jury in Charlotte, North Carolina, said GKN was guilty of a breach of contract over advertising arrangements at Meineke Discount Mufflers, its US specialist exhaust retailer. A group of Meineke's franchise operators claimed that the GKN subsidiary's in-house advertising agency had overcharged them and failed to generate new sales.
-- UK OPENS TELECOMS MARKET A YEAR BEFORE THE REST OF EU

Britain has opened its telecoms market to international companies after awarding licences to 44 operators, including AT&T of the US and the Global One alliance of Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom. The move, one year ahead of any of Britain's European Union neighbours, is designed to attract 5 billion stg of investment in the telecoms sector, and establish the UK as a regional communications hub.
-- WATCHDOG URGES REFORM AT LONDON METAL EXCHANGE

The Securities and Investments Board (SIB) has concluded its review of the workings of the London Metal Exchange (LME) instituted following the Sumitomo copper scandal. The SIB, the chief financial watchdog of the City of London, has recommended substantial changes to the operations of the LME, but rejected calls for wide-ranging reform. The main recommendation is a reorganisation of the board of the exchange, including an increase in its numbers.
-- EU TO BAN ANTIBIOTIC IN FEEDS

The European Union is to take action on an antibiotic commonly used in animal feeds which has been linked to an increase in resistance in animals to other antibiotics. The EU is set to ban the drug, called avoparcin, on the grounds that it could pose a risk to human health because its presence in the food chain diminishes the effectiveness of antibiotics in humans. Avoparcin has been widely used for 30 years as an aid to the digestive process in animals.
-- GM AND RENAULT IN PANEL VAN JOINT VENTURE

General Motors and Renault have agreed to a joint-venture for a new panel van to be built at GM's IBC Vehicles plant in Luton, Bedfordshire. The venture, which will create about 900 jobs at the plant, is part of a long-term co-operation agreement signed by the two automotive groups, which also provides for Renault to supply GM Europe with its existing Trafic panel van range, to be sold as the Vauxhall/Opel Arena.
-- GALLAHER TO CLOSE MANCHESTER CIGARETTE FACTORY

US-owned tobacco company Gallaher has announced plans to close a factory at Hyde, Manchester, with the loss of 950 jobs. Production in the UK will be concentrated at the company's plant in Antrim, Northern Ireland, which will get an extra 300 jobs. Expansion of the County Antrim plant will cost Gallaher an estimated 40 million stg.
-- CALENERGY POISED TO CAPTURE NORTHERN ELECTRIC

US utility CalEnergy is expected to succeed in its 782 million stg hostile bid for British regional electricity company Northern Electric, but only just. CalEnergy's offer closes on Friday and, according to information supplied to the Financial Times, the US predator is expected to take over 40 percent of Northern. Northern has conducted a strong defence against the bid, and observers say that about 30 percent of shareholders will remain loyal.
-- AIRTOURS IN 181 MILLION STG ITALIAN CRUISE LINE BID

Holiday tour operator Airtours has joined with its largest shareholder, Carnival Corporation, to offer 452 billion lira (181 million stg) for Italian cruise line Costa Crociere. In April this year US cruise line Carnival took a 29 percent stake in UK- based Airtours, and the Costa bid represents the first joint action taken by the new alliance.
-- ASDA TO EXPAND CAMPAIGN AGAINST PRICE-FIXING DEALS

Supermarket chain Asda, which has conducted high-profile campaigns against price-fixing arrangements in the book and drugs markets, is to target other products next year. Asda is currently involved in a campaign against the resale price mechanism on over-the-counter drugs, and also had success in opposing the net book agreement. The pledge to extend the campaign came as Asda reported a 15.8 percent rise in pre-tax profits before exceptionals, to 160.1 million stg.
-- TELEFONICA SET FOR FINAL SALE

The Spanish government is set to proceed with the sale of the remaining 21 percent stake it holds in national telecommunications operator Telefonica. The sale is expected to be completed by mid-February 1997, and will be Europe's third largest telecoms offering. The 21 percent stake would raise about 2.14 billion stg based on Telefonica's closing share price on Thursday.
